title: Nvidia Board Says Jensen Huang Won't Return as CEO
dek: Chair Harvey Jones shut down Huang's comeback bid on the earnings call.

facts.label: Q3 revenue, up 103% year over year

caption:
Jensen Huang offered to come back. Nvidia's board just said no.

On the Q3 earnings call, board chair Harvey Jones said the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." Huang resigned on November 12 after the board cited personal behavior that didn't match Nvidia's code of conduct, and he had floated a return on X just days ago. Interim CEO Colette Kress stays in charge while Heidrick & Struggles searches for a permanent chief.

The drama overshadowed a monster quarter: $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% from a year earlier. But an investigation into Huang's ties to an alleged Chinese asset, a new national security oversight committee and his upcoming testimony before Congress mean this isn't over.

Almost every AI tool runs on Nvidia chips, so who leads the company matters for everyone. We'll keep tracking it at AI Parabellum 👀

No comeback for Jensen Huang. Nvidia's board chair Harvey Jones said it plainly on the earnings call, and refused questions about Huang's exit or the ongoing investigation.

Colette Kress remains interim CEO as the hunt for a permanent leader begins, even as Nvidia posted a record $115.8B quarter.
